newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada expected to call election -- govt officials.
newsitem.headline: Canada expected to call election -- govt officials.

text.p: Canadian Prime Minister Jean Chretien was due to meet the country's governor-general on Sunday to ask him to dissolve parliament and pave the way for an early general election on June 2, government officials said.

"Prime Minister Chretien will meet with the Governor General at Rideau Hall at 12 noon (1600 GMT)," a statement from the prime minister's office said. Under Canada's parliamentary system, the prime minister must ask the governor-general to dissolve parliament so elections can be called.

Chretien, elected with a strong Liberal majority in October 1993, did not have to hold an election until October 1998, but officials said he decided to go for an earlier vote to capitalize on his standings in the polls.
"The election call will be made today," a government official said.

Chretien faces an opposition badly split into four camps -- with the Reform and Conservative parties carving up the right-wing vote, the Bloc Quebecois pushing for the separatist vote in Quebec and the New Democractic Party angling for the left.
